rationale: Use own colour and column colour set, excluding 0. In demonstration 2, columns containing only 1 and 2 map both to 8; demonstration 4 maps 3 to 9 in a {2,3} column and fills zeros with 3 in {1} columns.

Column sets excluding 0 determine replacements: {1,3} maps 0 to 5, {1,2,3} maps 0 to 8 and 2 to 7, and {2,3} maps 2 to 0. Demonstration 1 shows the first and third mappings; demonstration 2 shows the second.
Use column sets excluding 0. Demonstration 1 maps 2 to 9 in the {1,2} third column and maps 0 to 2 and 1 to 0 in {1,2,3} columns. Demonstration 2 also fills zeros with 2 in {1,3} columns.

Full 3x3 keys distinguish corner configurations. Demonstrations 1 and 8 map a top-left zero with an all-zero in-grid 2x2 neighbourhood to 6. Demonstration 8 maps the top-right 1, whose three in-grid neighbours are zero, to 9.

Demonstrations 1, 2 and 8 map the top-right zero to 4 when its entire in-grid 2x2 neighbourhood is zero. The full 3x3 key includes the top and right out-of-grid boundaries and distinguishes unchanged configurations.
Column sets excluding 0 determine outputs. Demonstration 1 maps 0 to 4 in {1,3}, 0 to 9 in {3}, and both 0 and 3 to 6 in {1,2,3}. Demonstration 4 repeats these mappings across several columns.

Use directional nearest nonzero colours. The changed zeros in demonstrations 1 and 5 have no colour above or right, nearest 3 below and 2 left, and become 9. Demonstration 6 maps a zero with no colour above or left, nearest 3 below and 1 right, to 5.

In demonstration 1, the two changed zeros are on the right edge away from corners, with every in-grid entry of their 3x3 neighbourhood zero. Their identical full neighbourhood keys map to 2; other demonstrated neighbourhoods remain unchanged.
Every demonstration replaces border colours 0, 1, 2 and 3 with 5, 6, 1 and 9 respectively, while interior pixels retain their colours. Own colour plus border flag expresses this directly.

Use own colour with both nonzero row and column sets. Demonstration 1 maps 2 to 3 when the row set is {1,2,3} and column set {1,2}; demonstration 2 maps 2 to 4 when both sets are {1,2,3}. Demonstration 6 maps 0 to 9 for row set {1} and column set {1,2,3}.
